sections.label: Judgment released to public
sections.summary: The full Judgment was released to the public on 11 October 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
sentences.text: The full Judgment was released to the public on 11 October 2019.

sections.label: High Court finds Lim and Low dishonest
sections.summary: The High Court found Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang dishonest, deceptive and in breach of duty to the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The High Court has found Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to be dishonest and deceptive, and to have failed in their duty to the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Indeed, Ms Sylvia Lim has admitted under oath that she had lied to the public.

sections.label: Surplus became deficit, friends profited
sections.summary: A $3.3 million surplus under previous management became a $2 million deficit by the new regime's third year, while their friends made millions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: A surplus of $3.3 million under the previous management, became a deficit of $2 million by the third year of the new regime.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And meanwhile, their friends made big profits running into millions of dollars.

sections.label: AHTC auditors issued disclaimer 2013
sections.summary: AHTC's own auditors first issued a disclaimer of opinion on its accounts in 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Many in the House will remember that it was AHTC's own auditors who first issued a disclaimer of opinion on its accounts back in 2013.

sections.label: AGO audit obstructed, shortcomings uncovered
sections.summary: Issues were not rectified, the 2014 Auditor-General audit was obstructed, and the 2015 report uncovered serious shortcomings casting doubt on public fund management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: But the issues they highlighted were not rectified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And so, in 2014, the Auditor-General carried out an audit, but like AHTC's own auditors, the Auditor-General's Office (AGO) was obstructed by the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Still, the 2015 AGO report uncovered serious shortcomings, which cast doubt on whether the Town Council was properly managing public funds.

sections.label: MND and HDB applied to High Court
sections.summary: Given the Workers' Party's inaction despite parliamentary debate, MND and then HDB applied to the High Court to deal with the matter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In view of the Workers' Party's inaction, despite the debate in Parliament, the Ministry of National Development (MND) and then the Housing and Development Board (HDB), applied to the High Court to deal with the matter.

sections.label: Court of Appeal finds breaches
sections.summary: The Court of Appeal found breaches of statutory requirements, lapses in internal controls, inadequate oversight of related party transactions, and failure to consider recovering sums from wrong payments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Court of Appeal said that it was clear that there had been breaches of the statutory requirements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It found lapses in internal controls, which exposed the Town Council to risk of loss of money or valuables; inadequate oversight of related party transactions, where key officers acted despite conflicts of interest; and that the Town Council had not seriously considered whether, and how, to recover possible sums due from wrong payments.

sections.label: Pervasive control failures
sections.summary: There were pervasive control failures across governance, financial control, financial reporting, procurement and records management.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Two, there were pervasive control failures cutting across the key areas of governance, financial control, financial reporting, procurement and records management.

sections.label: No urgency for tender waiver
sections.summary: Contrary to Workers' Party claims, there was no urgency warranting waiver of tenders for the MA and EMSU services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: One, contrary to the Workers' Party's claims, including claims made in Parliament, there was no urgency that warranted the waiver of the tenders for the MA and services under the Essential Maintenance Service Unit (EMSU).

sections.label: FMSS decision hidden from councillors
sections.summary: The two Workers' Party Members of Parliament decided on FMSS within days of the 2011 General Election and hid that from other councillors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The two Workers' Party Members of Parliament had already decided on FMSS within days of the 2011 General Election and had hidden that fact from other councillors.

sections.label: Low and Lim misled others
sections.summary: The Court found Low Thia Khiang and Sylvia Lim knew their tender waiver conduct was of questionable integrity and deliberately misled councillors, auditors, constituents and Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Court found that Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim had been fully aware that their conduct regarding the waiver of the tender was of "questionable integrity”.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: And to cover up their wrongdoing, they consciously and deliberately misled their own fellow town councillors, their own auditors, their constituents, and Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: As the High Court put it, there was a "deliberate and calculated" plan to, I quote, "cloak" and "camouflage" their wrongdoing.

sections.label: Lim asked to sanitise report
sections.summary: Sylvia Lim asked How Weng Fan and Danny Loh to sanitise the report on FMSS' appointment as MA so it could pass the auditors' eyes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Most disturbingly, Ms Sylvia Lim asked Ms How Weng Fan and Mr Danny Loh to sanitise the report on FMSS' appointment as MA so it could, I quote, "pass the auditors' eyes".

sections.label: Town Council press release tender claim
sections.summary: The Town Council's 5 August 2011 press release on FMSS's appointment falsely asserted there was no time to call a tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In the Town Council's press release on 5 August 2011 concerning the appointment of FMSS, they falsely asserted that there was no time to call a tender.

sections.label: Sylvia Lim tender urgency admission
sections.summary: Sylvia Lim admitted the urgency claim was not accurate and not true, and the Judge found waiver of tender not justified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Under cross-examination, Ms Sylvia Lim admitted that this was "not accurate", before finally admitting "it is not true", and that she knew it was not true.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Judge found that it was not sufficiently urgent to justify waiver of tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This means that when the Workers' Party told Parliament in 2015 that they waived tender because of urgency, they were misleading Parliament.

sections.label: Court findings on Low and Lim
sections.summary: The Court found Low Thia Khiang and Sylvia Lim breached fiduciary duties, were not honest, and questioned their integrity and candour.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Court found that Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim had breached their fiduciary duties, had not been honest and questioned their integrity and lack of candour and transparency.

sections.label: Recusal from Town Council affairs
sections.summary: The passage asks whether the severely judged Members of Parliament will be required to recuse themselves from Town Council affairs pending appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Is he going to require the Members of Parliament so severely judged and found wanting by the Court to recuse themselves from the Town Council’s affairs, pending the disposal of any appeal they may file?

sections.label: Removing Sylvia Lim as Vice Chairman
sections.summary: The passage asks whether Mr Faisal Manap will remove Ms Sylvia Lim as a Vice Chairman until any appeal is over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Until the appeal, if any, is over, will Mr Faisal Manap remove Ms Sylvia Lim as a Vice Chairman?

sections.label: KPMG finds AHTC lapses resolved
sections.summary: KPMG found last year that AHTC had finally resolved all lapses flagged in past audits since 2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Last year, KPMG found that AHTC had finally resolved all the lapses flagged in past audits since 2013.

sections.label: Court findings on WP leaders
sections.summary: The Court made serious statements that Low Thia Khiang and Sylvia Lim lacked candour, transparency, honesty and integrity in Town Council matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Court has made very serious and severe statements about Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It concluded that their conduct of Town Council matters lacked candour and transparency and that they had not acted honestly and with integrity.

sections.label: Workers' Party silence after judgment
sections.summary: Nearly four weeks after the judgment, the Workers' Party has said nothing and not apologised for shortcomings established by the Courts, AGO and KPMG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Almost four weeks have passed since the judgment was published.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: In all that time, the Workers' Party has said nothing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: They have not apologised for the shortcomings that the Courts – and before the Courts, AGO and KPMG – have established.

sections.label: Call for AHTC recusal
sections.summary: The High Court found Lim and Low dishonest and intransparent and in breach of fiduciary duties, so they should recuse themselves from AHTC financial matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The High Court has found Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to be dishonest and intransparent, and to have failed in their fiduciary duties to AHTC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Whether or not they will eventually appeal, they should recuse themselves from dealing with all financial matters in AHTC.

sections.label: Friends appointed without tender
sections.summary: They appointed their friends to run the Town Council without open tender and deliberately hid this plan from their own town councillors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Instead, they appointed their friends to run the Town Council without calling for an open tender, and deliberately hid this plan from their own town councillors.

sections.label: Upholding integrity and honesty
sections.summary: The speaker calls for upholding integrity, honesty and incorruptibility, and for AHTC to require Lim and Low to recuse themselves from financial matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: We must set ourselves as good examples, and uphold integrity, honesty, incorruptibility as our fundamental values.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I call on AHTC to discharge their responsibilities to their residents by requiring Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves from all matters relating to financial matters.

sections.label: Residents bear FMSS consequences
sections.summary: Under FMSS management the Town Council ran up deficits of up to $2 million by the third year while FMSS made a $3.2 million profit in its second year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The consequences of what the Workers' Party councillors have done, have fallen on the residents.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Under the management of FMSS, the Town Council ran up deficits of up to $2 million by the third year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Meanwhile, their friends, FMSS, made a profit of $3.2 million in their second year.

sections.label: Recusal from financial matters
sections.summary: The House asks Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves from financial matters until the Court case concludes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: All that this House is asking is for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves from dealing with or having oversight over financial matters, until the Court case is concluded.

sections.label: Court findings on contracts
sections.summary: The speaker says the Court found contracts worth millions were awarded under circumstances not quite justified.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked the point about the money has been lost.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I have mentioned in my speech that the Court's findings have been very clear that you have contracts worth millions of dollars which have been awarded under circumstances for which it was not quite justified.

sections.label: Court did not make law
sections.summary: The Court did not make new law; the law has been there.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The Court did not make new law; the law has been there.

sections.label: Emails revealed FMSS appointment
sections.summary: Documents were produced in Court proceedings, and emails revealed the truth on how FMSS was appointed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Many documents were produced during the Court of Appeal hearing and also during the various Court procedures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: It was only when the emails were produced, that it was revealed the truth on how FMSS was appointed.

sections.label: Recusal until Court case ends
sections.summary: The speaker cites serious findings in audit reports and Court findings, and asks both to recuse themselves from financial matters until the Court case ends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I have pointed out very serious findings in all the audit reports, in all the High Court findings, in the Court of Appeal findings, but both of you have just stood up to ask me a series of little details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: I have asked that all this House is asking is for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves from dealing with or having oversight over financial matters until the Court case is ended.

sections.label: Appeal to Court of Appeal
sections.summary: The speaker says they studied the judgment with lawyers and will appeal to the Court of Appeal by 11 November, asking the House to reject the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We have been studying the judgment with our lawyers since it was released.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: And I can inform the House today that we have decided to appeal the judgment to the Court of Appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: We are still within the timeframe to do so and it will be filed by 11 November.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Accordingly, the Deputy Prime Minister acted prematurely in his decision to file the Motion and I ask the House to reject it.

sections.label: Adjournment request and Sylvia Lim point
sections.summary: The Deputy Prime Minister asks what the adjournment is for, noting Ms Sylvia Lim said it was not proper for him to raise this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Deputy Prime Minister, what would you like the adjournment for?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: That is because the Member Ms Sylvia Lim has made the point that it was not proper for me to raise this.

sections.label: Foo Kon Tan disclaimers 2011 2012
sections.summary: From the first year auditors Foo Kon Tan audited the Town Council's accounts, in 2011 and 2012, four disclaimers were issued.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: You would know that from the very first year that you had auditors audit your Town Council's accounts, Foo Kon Tan, and that is in 2011, 2012, four disclaimers were issued by Foo Kon Tan.

sections.label: Thirteen disclaimers by 2012/2013
sections.summary: In 2012/2013 the same qualifiers were made, and by that time 13 disclaimers had been made.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: In the following year, in 2012/2013, the same qualifiers were made; in fact, by that time, 13 disclaimers had been made.

sections.label: PwC on missing FMSS emails
sections.summary: PwC said no single email on matters relating to FMSS's takeover of MA and EMSU contract services was given to it for review.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: PwC says, and I quote, "No single email on matters in relation to the takeover of the MA and EMSU contract services by FMSS, including the termination of CPG, the award of contracts to FMSS and all FMSS' performance of works, were given to us for our review, though in our view, such emails ought to exist." This is six years after FMSS was appointed.

sections.label: Conflicted persons payment approval risk
sections.summary: Paragraph 13 of the summary states conflicted persons in the approval process for payments to FMSS and FMSI created an inherent risk of overpayment without safeguards.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health and Law (Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai)
sentences.text: Paragraph 13 of the summary, it says, "The involvement of conflicted persons in the approval process for payments to FMSS and FMSI created an inherent risk of overpayment in the absence of safeguards.

sections.label: KPMG report on deleted documents
sections.summary: KPMG's 31 October 2016 report noted difficulties getting information from AHTC, and deleted documents and archives were found on devices.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Yes, when KPMG was appointed, there was a media release dated 1 June 2016, where it said, "AHTC's town councillors had decided that AHTC would focus its fullest attention on KPMG." I think that is what Ms Sylvia Lim had referred to, in terms of the duplication of work.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But in a report dated 31 October 2016 by KPMG, KPMG itself noted difficulties in getting information and documents out of AHTC.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: When KPMG examined the electronic devices of Town Council staff and FMSS employees, they found that documents and archives had been deleted.

sections.label: AHTC councillors refused KPMG interviews
sections.summary: Elected AHTC councillors, including Sylvia Lim and Low Thia Khiang, refused to take part in oral interviews and did not cooperate with KPMG.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They wanted to have oral interviews so that they can ask questions and you answer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But Ms Sylvia Lim will remember that she and Mr Low Thia Khiang and, in fact, every single elected councillor of AHTC, refused to take part in the interview, refused to cooperate with KPMG.

sections.label: Related party fees to AHPETC
sections.summary: Auditor Foo Kon Tan Grant Thornton and the 2015 AGO report noted AHPETC paid substantial sums to related parties in FY2012/2013.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: First, your own auditor Foo Kon Tan Grant Thornton in their FY2012/2013 report, at page 4, says, "The Town Council had not made available to us details of the project management service fees paid to a related party." In the 2015 AGO report, it says, "We note that AHPETC has entered into a number of related party transactions whereby substantial sums were paid to related parties in FY2012/2013.

sections.label: Probity of MPs with public funds
sections.summary: The House must agree on probity standards for MPs, and the question is whether Workers' Party town councillors found dishonest should keep control of public funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: This House needs to agree on the principles that all Members of Parliament must adhere to and the standards of probity required of all Members of Parliament in dealing with public funds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: There are serious issues of probity, accountability and the handling of public funds that must be addressed now even while the appeal is being dealt with.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: The question is: what should be done, what should happen between now and the time when the appeal is decided?

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: So, in the interim, my question is: should the Workers' Party town councillors who have been found to have acted dishonestly and have been found to be in breach of their duties, whose conduct was found to be egregious, should they continue to have access to and control of public funds?

sections.label: Motion rejected during appeal period
sections.summary: The Motion is rejected as inappropriate because the case involving Sylvia Lim and Low Thia Khiang is still within the appeal period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I also reject this Motion as it is not appropriate for it to be moved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: This is because the case involving Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang is still within the period allowed for appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: The Court’s decision was released on 11 October 2019 and the appeal period will only end on 11 November.

sections.label: FMSS appointed without tender
sections.summary: The High Court judgment shows Sylvia Lim and Low Thia Khiang knowingly engineered FMSS's appointment as AHTC managing agent without tender and concealed the reason.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The judgment of the High Court shows not only that Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang knew that appointing FMSS without a tender would be wrong, but that they went ahead anyway in a considered, calculated manner to accomplish it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang engineered a series of steps to ensure the appointment of FMSS as the MA of AHTC without tender. "They made it a fait accompli" – those are the words of the Judge – which allowed FMSS to charge higher rates to the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They took steps to carefully conceal the true reason of the appointment and this included concealing it even from their own town councillors.

sections.label: AGO audit missing documents
sections.summary: The AGO's 6 February 2015 report said the Town Council could not provide some documents concerning transactions after AHPETC took over.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Subsequently, as you know, the AGO came in to audit and, in its report dated 6 February 2015, when they looked back, they said, "Town Council could not provide some documents required during the current audit that concerned transactions taking place after AHPETC had taken over from the previous Town Council.

sections.label: PwC notes missing Town Council documents
sections.summary: PwC said the Town Council did not provide internal notes and emails on tender awards and related disclosures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In its report to AGO which formed part of the AGO report, PwC noted, and I quote, "In particular, we would point out that the Town Council did not provide us with internal notes and correspondence, including emails, which may shed light on: the process leading to the award of tenders/contracts; and evidencing the deliberation/evaluation of the award of tender/contracts…disclosure of interest or are otherwise related to approval for transactions chosen." Very clear statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And I would have thought that if one was trying to audit the propriety of payments to FMSS to check if its transactions and the approval of FMSS contract was proper, those were the first place you would look and, indeed, Ms Sylvia Lim will remember that in Court, what was then produced was an email of 3 August, where just prior to the approval at the Town Council's meeting on 4 August there was an email from you asking for Ms How Weng Fan and the late Mr Danny Loh to sanitise the auditors' report, sanitise the very report that was meant to recommend the appointment of FMSS and those were the documents that were sought by the auditors, right from the beginning.

sections.label: PwC says no emails produced
sections.summary: PwC states no internal emails or correspondence were produced, which the speaker calls a pattern blocking disclosure.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: PwC is saying not a single email, internal correspondence was produced.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, it is a clear, consistent pattern of behaviour designed to block disclosure of the relevant documents and information, information which would allow a forensic inquiry into what had happened and what you had done.

sections.label: Independent Panel sues AHTC leaders
sections.summary: After a protracted process, the AHTC-appointed Independent Panel decided to sue Sylvia Lim, Low Thia Khiang and others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim's email to Ms How Weng Fan and Mr Danny Loh is dated 3 August 2011.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And so eventually, after an unnecessarily protracted process, the Independent Panel, chosen and appointed by AHTC and which Mr Pritam Singh quite rightly says comprised "eminent" persons, decided to sue Ms Sylvia Lim, Mr Low Thia Khiang and others, on behalf of AHTC and we now know the outcome of that.

sections.label: Statements made in press and Parliament
sections.summary: The passage lists a press release, two parliamentary debates and an open letter where statements were made.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: In a press release to the public dated 5 August 2011, the very next day after the fateful Town Council's meeting; in Parliament during the 2013 debate on the Ministerial Statement on Town Councils; again, in Parliament in February 2015 during a debate on the AGO report; and in an open letter to residents in June 2015 prior to the last General Election.

sections.label: Workers' Party wrote to How Weng Fan
sections.summary: The Workers' Party wrote to Ms How Weng Fan on 19 May saying her company would be appointed MA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Workers' Party had also already written to Ms How Weng Fan as early as 19 May, that is, barely a week after General Election 2011 – wrote to her to say that her company would be appointed as MA of the Town Council and this is well before the Workers' Party even had any conversation with CPG.

sections.label: Judge criticises FMSS contingency claim
sections.summary: The Judge said presenting FMSS as a contingency was an attempt to camouflage its true motive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Not surprisingly, the Judge had strong words about the Workers' Party seeking to present FMSS as a contingency, as a reason both to the public as well as in justification for not having a tender and he said, and I quote, "this was nothing more than an attempt to varnish the plan with a veneer of credibility in order to camouflage its true motive".

sections.label: Town Council tender timing
sections.summary: The Town Council had sufficient time to call a tender but did not want to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Town Council had sufficient time to call a tender; it just did not want to do so.

sections.label: Judge on AIM withdrawal
sections.summary: The Judge concluded AIM's withdrawal did not precipitate the defendants' conduct and they had sufficient time to call a tender.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Judge, having heard from Ms Sylvia Lim in Court on this issue, concluded, and I quote, "AIM's withdrawal in no way precipitated the defendants' course of conduct leading to the waiver of the tender...  that   had sufficient time to call for a tender notwithstanding AIM's withdrawal".

sections.label: Sanitising draft report request
sections.summary: The Court found Ms Sylvia Lim asked Ms How Weng Fan and Mr Danny Loh to sanitise the draft report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First, the Court found that, in ensuring that the appointment of FMSS would pass muster, Ms Sylvia Lim asked for Ms How Weng Fan and Mr Danny Loh to "sanitise" the draft report – I mentioned that earlier, let me come back to it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So that, in your own words, Ms Sylvia Lim, it will "pass the auditors' eyes"; your email of 3 August 2011.

sections.label: Judge on report truthfulness
sections.summary: The Judge found the report was not truthful and painted a wholly inaccurate picture.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: And do not take my word for it, look at what the Judge had found about that report.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: It said, "It was not truthful and painted a wholly inaccurate picture" and it "sought to cloak the appointment of FMSS with a veneer of propriety”.

sections.label: Deliberate move to conceal
sections.summary: The Court found a deliberate and calculated move to keep CPG and the Town Council in the dark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Court found that there was, and I quote again, "a deliberate and calculated move" to keep CPG and the rest of the Town Council in the dark about the plan to appoint FMSS without a tender being called.

sections.label: Keeping truth from councillors
sections.summary: Ms Sylvia Lim kept the truth from fellow town councillors, who include fellow Members of Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: But what is even more stark about this episode is that not only did the Workers' Party subvert the entire system of accountability within the Town Council and made use of the councillors to suit their own personal and political agenda, but also that Ms Sylvia Lim kept the truth from her fellow town councillors.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: They might well have had their own concerns about the political allegiances of CPG or AIM, but the town councillors are Workers' Party members from their own party or supporters, and they include fellow Members of Parliament in this House.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: That they felt they had to mislead their own colleagues to get FMSS appointed without tender, I think, speaks volumes.

sections.label: Motion on financial oversight recusal
sections.summary: The Motion requires only recusal from financial oversight and control, not resignation or stepping down from all town councillor functions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: The Motion does not require anyone to resign, to step down, not even to refrain from all functions of a town councillor, but only that which relates to financial oversight and control.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: Can Mr Faisal Manap explain why that is not in the best interest of the Town Council and the residents, why that is not the proper and decent thing to do, so that you have assurance that whatever is the outcome on the appeal, your interest and those of your residents are safeguarded?

sections.label: Wait for Court of Appeal
sections.summary: The speaker calls for waiting until the Court of Appeal result before deciding actions, asking for a narrow recusal over financial oversight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Additionally, I believe everyone in this Chamber understands that the Court of Appeal can overturn the current findings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: Hence, being a responsible Chair of AHTC, based on the reasonings I have stated above, my call is to wait until the result of the appeal is out before deciding on any actions to be taken.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: First of all, Mr Faisal Manap, there is no suggestion that you reverse the mandate that has been given.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: We are asking for a narrow recusal over financial oversight.

sections.label: No support for Motion
sections.summary: The speaker stands firm on waiting for the Court of Appeal before taking action and states clearly that he does not support the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: The finding can be overturned by the Court of Appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: So, I stand firm on my call to wait for the Court of Appeal, before I decide to take any actions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edwin Tong Chun Fai
sentences.text: So, is Mr Faisal Manap saying that absolutely nothing at all will be done by AHTC, notwithstanding the grave and serious judgment that has been released by the High Court, which AHTC, and I hear the Workers' Party, recognised and accepted, that nothing will be done in the interim?

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap
sentences.text: I have stated clearly that I do not support this Motion.

sections.label: High Court AHTC judgment findings
sections.summary: Justice Kannan Ramesh's 11 October judgment found Sylvia Lim and Low Thia Khiang breached fiduciary duties and acted dishonestly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In the AHTC case, High Court Judge Kannan Ramesh gave a judgment on 11 October, which found that two Workers' Party Members of Parliament, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang were in breach of their fiduciary duties and, due to that, they are responsible for the losses incurred by AHTC.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: In fact, the High Court found that they misled their colleagues and found that they had acted dishonestly.

sections.label: Call for Lim and Low recusal
sections.summary: It is unclear whether AHTC asked Sylvia Lim and Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves until the case outcome is clear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: At this point of time, and after the High Court gave its ruling, we are still unclear whether AHTC has taken the appropriate actions by asking both Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves until the outcome of the case is clear.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: However, for the sake of the residents, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang should do the right thing by recusing themselves.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Not for them to resign, but to recuse themselves.

sections.label: Faisal Manap asked on judgment facts
sections.summary: Faisal Manap is asked whether he agrees with the High Court's facts on the no-tender contract and FMSS appointment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: Does Mr Faisal Manap, as the Chairman of AHTC, agree with the facts contained in the High Court's judgment?

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: I used the word "facts" and not "judgment" because I understand that the Workers' Party will make an appeal on the High Court's judgment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: So, the Judge has found that, based on facts, the actions of Members of Parliament, Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang, who awarded a contract without calling a tender, gave a misleading picture about the appointment of FMSS.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower and National Development (Mr Zaqy Mohamad)
sentences.text: So, does Mr Faisal Manap, as the Chairman of AHTC, agree or disagree with the facts presented in the Court's judgment on 11 October 2019, which found that both of them have acted in breach of their fiduciary duties towards AHTC?

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In its judgment, the High Court stated that AHTC had decided not to call an open tender without justifiable reasons, and appointed FMSS as the management company.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The High Court has found that Mr Low Thia Khiang and Ms Sylvia Lim had breached their fiduciary duties, and Mr Pritam Singh has breached his duties of skill and care to AHTC.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: The Court has also found that Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang had deliberately kept the matter of appointing a new MA in the dark and made misleading statements.

sections.label: High Court verdict on MPs
sections.summary: The High Court ruled that three Worker's Party MPs must bear legal responsibility for the Town Council's loss.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Home Affairs and National Development (Ms Sun Xueling)
sentences.text: In October this year, the High Court passed a verdict that the three Worker's Party Members of Parliament must bear legal responsibility for the loss suffered by the Town Council.

sections.label: Potong Pasir 2011 election margin
sections.summary: In the 2011 General Elections, Potong Pasir was regained by a margin of 114 votes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In the 2011 General Elections, we regained Potong Pasir by the slimmest of margins – 114 votes.

sections.label: Potong Pasir arrears reduction
sections.summary: Potong Pasir Division's households in Service and Conservancy charge arrears fell from over 400 in 2011 to under 100 today.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: In 2011, we had more than 400 households in arrears of Service and Conservancy charges for more than three months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Today, we have less than 100 such families in Potong Pasir Division in similar arrears and the total amount is below $100,000.

sections.label: Support for accountability Motion
sections.summary: The speaker fully supports the Motion, stressing the need to do things right and ensure accountability in Town Council duties.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: And more importantly, we must do it right and ensure accountability in our duties in the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: It is in this context, Mr Speaker, that I fully support the Motion.

sections.label: Appeal on key findings
sections.summary: The position is that some key findings will be taken on appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Again, our position is that some of these key findings, we are going to take it on appeal.

sections.label: Auditors given full IT access
sections.summary: The speaker recalls the General Manager saying auditors had full access to the IT system, refuting any suggestion of hiding things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: On the second point on whether the Town Council had been forthcoming with information for its own auditors, I recalled at that point in time a conversation which I had with our General Manager, who told me that, actually, the auditors were given full access to our information technology (IT) system to search for any information that they wanted.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, I think it is important that I put on record that that was what I recalled when I asked her about the auditors' comment, that was what she told me.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Last of all, regarding the AGO audit, he did cite that the AGO had said that they had asked for certain documents which should exist.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: So, I would refute any suggestion that we tried to hide things from the auditors.

sections.label: Support for Motion's first part
sections.summary: He supports the Motion's first part but questions the need for a Motion with no legal force given the Minister's existing powers under the Town Councils Act.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I clearly support this first part of the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I wish to speak on this Motion because I am unsure of the need for this Motion, which has no legal force when passed, given the powers already vested in the Minister through the Town Councils Act to order AHTC to take necessary and swift actions.

sections.label: Section 43(d) remedial powers
sections.summary: Section 43(d) lets the Minister order a Town Council to take remedial action, was added in 2017, and the defendants plan to appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Under section 43(d) of the Act, it is expressively provided that if the Minister is of the opinion that there are deficiencies identified in the conduct of the affairs of the Town Council and/or an irregularity has occurred or is occurring in the financial affairs of the Town Council, the Minister may, by order, in writing, require the Town Council to "take specified remedial action to address the deficiencies and take specified action to correct the irregularity or to guard against the recurrence of irregularities or both." This entire section was an amendment added to the Act and passed by this House only two years back in 2017.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Court proceeding, as I understand according to the Administration of Justice Protection Act, only concludes when all issues relating to the assessment of damages and Court proceedings are heard and finally decided.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, it is clear that if a legal proceeding of this case is still afoot, the defendants are also entitled to launch an appeal, which we have just heard from Ms Sylvia Lim that they will be doing so.

sections.label: Reasons for abstaining on Motion
sections.summary: He abstains because he cannot understand a Motion with no legal force when the Town Councils Act already grants the Minister such powers, and debate may be seen as interfering with due process.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This privilege to serve comes with the commensurate responsibility that I take dutifully and seriously to add value to the discourse in this House as a non-partisan voice, hopefully in a considered manner and hopefully most of the time, to the best of my ability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It is with this same consideration that my abstention to this Motion today, when called for a vote, is premised on: (a) my inability to understand the call for action through this Motion with no legal force when they exist in an enforceable pathway in accordance with the rule of law under the Town Councils Act, which I believe already grants the Minister powers to do the same as proposed in part (iv) of the Motion; and (b) my inability to raise a concern that the debate in the House from the judgment of a Court proceeding that has yet to be fully concluded, as indicated in parts (ii) and (iii) of the Motion, may be perceived as interference of due process in the administration of justice.

sections.label: Judgment on fiduciary duty breach
sections.summary: The judgment finds Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang seriously breached fiduciary duty by planning to appoint FMSS as MA without a tender, harming AHTC and residents.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The judgment does find a serious breach of fiduciary duty on the part of the hon Members Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The breach is because they had planned to appoint FMSS as MA without calling a tender.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The breach is found to have harmed the interest of AHTC and, by extension, residents.

sections.label: Abstention as non-elected Member
sections.summary: He agrees Parliament must hold Members to high integrity standards but is uncomfortable as a non-elected Member joining a political resolution, so he will abstain if there is a Division.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Therefore, while I agree with the principle that Parliament must hold all Members to a high standard of integrity and must examine Members who fall short, I am uncomfortable as a non-elected Member in participating in what may be a political resolution.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Walter Theseira (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Hence, I will abstain from the Motion, if there is Division.

sections.label: Proper conduct after judgment
sections.summary: He asks what is right and proper for a person holding fiduciary duties as director, charitable institution head, trustee or elected town councillor once a judgment has been made.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are not talking about when allegations are made, no matter how strongly proven those allegations may be before the suit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: We are talking about when a judgment has been made, what should the person in the shoes of a director of a company, as the head of a charitable institution, as a trustee, as a town councillor elected by the public holding statutory responsibilities, having fiduciary duties, sitting in this very House, what is the right and proper thing to do?

sections.label: Duties of Members of Parliament
sections.summary: The House is asking what Members with duties under the Town Councils Act should do to safeguard public monies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: Quite apart from what regulatory powers there may be in this case or in future cases, we are really asking here in his House, not asking what directors outside this House should be doing; not asking what trustees outside should be doing, but what Members of this House reposed with the duties under the Town Councils Act to safeguard public monies.

sections.label: Watching town councillors' action
sections.summary: For almost four weeks, the public and commentators have watched what action town councillors subject to High Court findings would take to safeguard public funds.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: In fact, for the last almost four weeks, all of us, members of the public and commentators, have been watching and listening and looking out for what action town councillors subject to such findings by the High Court would take, at the very minimum, to safeguard public funds, to assure the people that they are responsible for, pending the appeal which they will no doubt fight, as Ms Sylvia Lim has indicated.

sections.label: Recusal from financial duties
sections.summary: The passage asks the person to recuse from financial duties, not all Town Council duties, that the Judges' findings focused on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: At the very least, recuse yourself, not from all Town Council duties but from financial duties for which the Judges' findings focused on.

sections.label: FMSS appointment motivated politically
sections.summary: The High Court found the appointment of FMSS as MA was clearly motivated by political consideration, including a misguided sense of loyalty to trust supporters.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The High Court judgment has found, in this case, that the appointment of FMSS as MA was clearly motivated by political consideration, including a misguided sense of loyalty to trust the supporters.

sections.label: Friends set up FMSS company
sections.summary: A plan involved getting friends to incorporate FMSS days after the 2011 General Elections with paid-up capital of $450,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: And, so, they devised a plan to ensure that they will get what they want.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: This involved getting their friends to incorporate and set up a company FMSS just days after the results of 2011 General Elections with a substantial paid-up capital of $450,000.

sections.label: Court found dishonesty and smokescreens
sections.summary: The Court found dishonesty and fanning of smokescreens, and that the report on FMSS's appointment was not truthful and painted a wholly inaccurate picture.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The Court found not negligence, carelessness or breach of contract but dishonesty and fanning of smokescreens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The public, our Parliament, were all misled deliberately.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The High Court found that the report prepared on the appointment of FMSS as MA for the Town Council, setting out the reasons for waiver of tender, under the instructions of Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang, was, I quote, "not truthful and painted a wholly inaccurate picture".

sections.label: Auditors found FMSS charged more
sections.summary: PwC and KPMG had previously found FMSS charged more than CPG.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The auditors, PwC and KPMG, have all previously found FMSS to have charged more than CPG.

sections.label: Damages, deficits and FMSS profits
sections.summary: Damages are subject to further proceedings, and residents' interests and public funds were abused while AHPETC ran deficits and FMSS profited.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: The issue of damages, what needs to be recovered, is subject to further proceedings before the Court.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: I will make the point but not comment further about the details.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development and Second Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
sentences.text: But it is clear that residents' interests, public funds were abused as a result of the MA contracts with FMSS while FMSS, in turn, had profited handsomely.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: Within the first full year of the Workers' Party's management, AHPETC, as it then was, ran an operating deficit of $1.5 million, which widened to a deficit of $2 million in the second year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: In stark contrast, Workers' Party's friends in FMSS made $1.5 million in profits in the first full year, which shot up to some $3.2 million in the second year.

sections.label: High Court found breach of duties
sections.summary: The High Court found the defendants in breach of legal duties, including fiduciary duties of loyalty to the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: How is this protecting the interests of residents and safeguarding public funds?

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: It, therefore, comes as no surprise that the High Court had found the defendants to be in breach of legal duties, including their fiduciary duties of loyalty owed to the Town Council.

sections.label: Implicated MPs should recuse themselves
sections.summary: Members of Parliament implicated should recuse themselves from all Town Council financial transactions pending any appeal.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The right and proper thing to do is for the Members of Parliament implicated in this matter to recuse themselves from all financial transactions of the Town Council pending any appeal.

sections.label: Court found Lim and Low dishonest
sections.summary: The High Court found Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang acted dishonestly, lacked integrity and candour, and knew their conduct was of questionable legality.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The High Court judgment has found that Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang acted dishonestly, in breach of fiduciary duty, that their conduct lacked integrity and candour, and that they were fully aware that their conduct was of questionable legality.

sections.label: Judgment findings stand until overturned
sections.summary: A judgment's findings stand until and unless they are overturned.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: As all the lawyers in this room know, a judgment, once given, until and unless overturned, the findings stand.

sections.label: Workers' Party moral authority
sections.summary: The Workers' Party would have no moral authority to ask officials to stand aside during pending inquiries or appeals.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: What it also means is that the next time there is any incident and there is an inquiry pending, the Workers’ Party has no moral authority to ask for any official to stand down or stand aside whilst the case is being heard, or whilst the matter goes for appeal.

sections.label: Motion for recusal pending appeal
sections.summary: The Motion asks Workers' Party members to recuse themselves from Town Council financial matters pending appeal, citing transparency and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They gave them a mandate to run the Town Council.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They did not give them a mandate to breach their fiduciary duties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: They did not give them a mandate to act dishonestly and they did not give them a mandate to act with a lack of integrity and candor.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, what you have is that in 2019, you have a Court judgment which has made these findings and the issue is, as my colleague Mr Desmond Lee has highlighted, what do you do between now and the time of the appeal?

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: All that this Motion asks is that they do the appropriate thing, which is to recuse themselves from all matters relating to and oversight of financial matters in the Town Council pending the appeal.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: This goes to transparency, accountability and good governance.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, if, as the Workers’ Party says, they stand for transparency, accountability and good governance, then there should be no objection to this Motion.

sections.label: Workers' Party on integrity standards
sections.summary: The Workers' Party agrees with the Motion's first limb on integrity and accountability, and states it did not knowingly mislead the House in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: At the outset, I have heard it from a few speakers, and I think it is important to put the position on record – the Workers' Party does not disagree with the first limb of the Motion which calls on the House to affirm the vital importance of Members of Parliament maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On that note, for the record, in 2015, I did not knowingly and deliberately mislead this House.

sections.label: AHTC unqualified audited report
sections.summary: AHTC's auditors submitted an unqualified audited report to the Council, forwarded to MND for tabling in Parliament.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For the information of the House, for the latest annual report, AHTC's auditors have submitted an unqualified audited report to the Council which has been forwarded to MND for onward tabling to Parliament.

sections.label: Workers' Party voting against Motion
sections.summary: The Workers' Party Members of Parliament will unanimously vote against the Motion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party has read the Motion carefully and all the Workers’ Party Members of Parliament will unanimously vote against it.

sections.label: Court findings and public position
sections.summary: It asks whether a person found by a Court to have breached fiduciary duty and lacked integrity should remain in position while findings stand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Let us just have a look at something else and not pay attention to this.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: We are talking about something else which is simply this: when you have somebody in a public position, if a Court has found that they have done something wrong, there has been a breach of fiduciary duty, lack of integrity, that they have not acted with appropriate candor, should that person remain in position whilst those findings are there whilst they still stand and whether or not an appeal is pending?

sections.label: Town Council recusal motion
sections.summary: A councillor could raise recusal at the November meeting, and the Motion calls on the Town Council to act without Parliament forcing it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh
sentences.text: If a town councillor at the next quarterly meeting in November brings this issue up and the Council determines that, yes, it is a recusal that is in order, then Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang, they will have to recuse themselves because that is what the Council decides.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: The Motion calls on the Town Council to do certain things.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: So, the Motion, if passed, this Parliament is not forcing the Town Council to do anything, but it is calling upon it to do something.

sections.label: Findings of fact stand
sections.summary: The findings of fact will stand until reversed by the Appeals Court.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
sentences.text: The findings of what had happened, being as they are, findings of fact, these findings will stand until they are reversed by the Appeals Court.

sections.label: Workers' Party recusal question
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Workers' Party is prepared for Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang to recuse themselves from all AHTC financial decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Given the severity of the judgment, is the Workers' Party prepared to have Ms Sylvia Lim and Mr Low Thia Khiang recuse themselves from all financial decisions of AHTC?

sections.label: Government concerns and principles
sections.summary: The Government will express concerns to AHTC's Independent Panel, and Workers' Party Members raised no point on the proposed basic principles.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: Given this position, the Government will be forced to express its concerns to AHTC's own Independent Panel.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: On the second part, the second key question which I have raised, which is to ask the Workers' Party Members whether they would join with the Government Members of Parliament to set out some basic principles for the conduct of Members of Parliament, both inside and outside the House – to be honest in our dealings with our fellow town councillors, to be honest in our statements in Parliament or, indeed, in any forum, including the Courts, to put the interests of the residents we represent above that of ourselves and our friends.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: None of the Workers' Party Members, unfortunately, raised any point about the basic principles that we have set out.

sentences.speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
sentences.text: After all, would the Workers' Party not agree that maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability are at the core of a First-World Parliament or have you forgotten about First-World Parliament?

sections.label: Parliament motion on AHTC judgment
sections.summary: The motion affirms integrity standards, notes the judgment against Ms Lim and Mr Low, and calls on AHTC to require their recusal from financial matters.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Question is, "That this Parliament: (i) affirms the vital importance of Members of Parliament maintaining high standards of integrity and accountability; (ii) notes the Judgment in Aljunied-Hougang Town Council and anor v Lim Swee Lian Sylvia and ors and anor suit   SGHC 241, where, amongst other things, the Court held that: (a) Ms Sylvia Lim ("Ms Lim") and Mr Low Thia Khiang ("Mr Low") had acted dishonestly and in breach of their fiduciary duties, and their conduct lacked integrity and candour; and (b) Ms Lim and Mr Low were fully aware that their conduct was of questionable legality; (iii) notes that Ms Lim remains Vice-Chairman of Aljunied-Hougang Town Council, and Mr Low remains an elected member of Aljunied-Hougang Town Council; and (iv) calls on Aljunied-Hougang Town Council to discharge their responsibilities to their residents by requiring Ms Lim and Mr Low to recuse themselves from all matters relating to, and oversight over, financial matters." Mr Pritam Singh, you have claimed a Division, would you like to proceed with the Division?

sections.label: Voting results declared
sections.summary: The voting results are 52 Ayes, nine Noes, and two Abstentions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will proceed to declare the voting results now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There are 52 "Ayes", nine "Noes", and two "Abstentions".
